     2	# About This Monorepo
     3	
     4	This monorepo contains a set of dev-friendly, framework agnostic components offering 3 main capabilities:
     5	
     6	- **Instructor for PHP** - structured data extraction in PHP - powered by LLMs, designed for simplicity, transparency, and control; supports custom LLM output processors (not just JSON),
     7	- **Polyglot for PHP** - unified LLM API - write code once, deploy with any LLM provider: OpenAI chat completions API, OpenAI responses API, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama, etc.; you can write own LLM drivers,
     8	- **Agent SDK for PHP** - lightweight but powerful agent SDK, supports custom tools, lifecycle hooks, subagents, context management, custom stop / continuation criteria, observability via events, packaged capabilities, agent templates, session management, and more.
     9	
    10	Framework integration packages:
    11	
    12	- **Laravel Package** - first-party Laravel integration for facades, HTTP transport, native agents, telemetry, logging, and testing
    13	- **Symfony Package** - first-party batteries-included Symfony integration package, currently being introduced under `packages/symfony`
    14	
    15	## Read More
    16	
    17	- Official website https://instructorphp.com
    18	- Docs website (Mintlify) https://docs.instructorphp.com
    19	- Docs (Github Pages) https://cognesy.github.io/instructor-php/
    20	
    21	## Overview of Capabilities
    22	
    23	The library offers a set of small, focused building blocks.
    24	
    25	### Structured output
    26	
    27	Purpose: turn messy model output into typed PHP data.
    28	Benefit: you stop hand-parsing JSON or text before using LLM results.
    29	
    30	```php
    31	use Cognesy\Instructor\StructuredOutput;
    32	
    33	final class Person {
    34	    public string $name;
    35	    public int $age;
    36	}
    37	
    38	$person = StructuredOutput::using('openai')
    39	    ->with(messages: 'Jason is 28 years old.', responseModel: Person::class)
    40	    ->get();
    41	```
    42	
    43	Detailed docs: [packages/instructor/docs/](packages/instructor/docs/)
    44	
    45	### Unified inference
    46	
    47	Purpose: call different LLM providers through one API.
    48	Benefit: switch providers without rewriting request code.
    49	
    50	```php
    51	use Cognesy\Polyglot\Inference\Inference;
    52	
    53	$text = Inference::using('openai')
    54	    ->withMessages('Say hello in one sentence.')
    55	    ->get();
    56	```
    57	
    58	Detailed docs: [packages/polyglot/docs/](packages/polyglot/docs/)
    59	
    60	### Embeddings
    61	
    62	Purpose: generate vectors through the same provider layer.
    63	Benefit: keep retrieval and inference in one stack.
    64	
    65	```php
    66	use Cognesy\Polyglot\Embeddings\Embeddings;
    67	
    68	$vectors = Embeddings::using('openai')
    69	    ->withInputs(['hello world'])
    70	    ->vectors();
    71	```
    72	
    73	Detailed docs: [packages/polyglot/docs/](packages/polyglot/docs/)
    74	
    75	### Agents SDK
    76	
    77	Purpose: build tool-using agents as a simple loop over state.
    78	Benefit: add tools and control flow without inventing your own agent runtime first.
    79	
    80	```php
    81	use Cognesy\Agents\AgentLoop;
    82	use Cognesy\Agents\Data\AgentState;
    83	
    84	$result = AgentLoop::default()->execute(
    85	    AgentState::empty()->withUserMessage('What is 2+2?')
    86	);
    87	```
    88	
    89	Detailed docs: [packages/agents/docs/](packages/agents/docs/)
    90	
    91	### Code agent bridges
    92	
    93	Purpose: drive external coding agents like Codex, Claude Code, and OpenCode from PHP.
    94	Benefit: automate reviews, summaries, and coding workflows through one interface.
    95	
    96	```php
    97	use Cognesy\AgentCtrl\AgentCtrl;
    98	
    99	$response = AgentCtrl::codex()->execute('Summarize this repository.');
   100	```
   101	
   102	Detailed docs: [packages/agent-ctrl/docs/](packages/agent-ctrl/docs/)
   103	
   104	### Framework integration
   105	
   106	Purpose: install framework-native runtime wiring instead of assembling your own glue.
   107	Benefit: get a supported bundle or package surface for container bindings, events, observability, and testing.
   108	
   109	- Laravel package: [packages/laravel/](packages/laravel/)
   110	- Symfony package: [packages/symfony/](packages/symfony/)
   111	
   112	Symfony docs highlights:
   113	
   114	- quickstart: [packages/symfony/docs/quickstart.md](packages/symfony/docs/quickstart.md)
   115	- configuration: [packages/symfony/docs/configuration.md](packages/symfony/docs/configuration.md)
   116	- operations: [packages/symfony/docs/operations.md](packages/symfony/docs/operations.md)
   117	- migration: [packages/symfony/docs/migration.md](packages/symfony/docs/migration.md)

   120	## What is Instructor?
   121	
   122	Instructor is a library that allows you to extract structured, validated data from multiple types of inputs: text, images or OpenAI style chat sequence arrays. It is powered by Large Language Models (LLMs).
   123	
   124	Instructor simplifies LLM integration in PHP projects. It handles the complexity of extracting structured data from LLM outputs, so you can focus on building your application logic and iterate faster.
   125	
   126	Instructor for PHP is inspired by the [Instructor](https://jxnl.github.io/instructor/) library for Python created by [Jason Liu](https://twitter.com/jxnlco).
   127	
   128	![image](docs/images/concept.png)
   129	
   130	Here's a simple CLI demo app using Instructor to extract structured data from text:
   131	
   132	![image](docs/images/extraction.gif)
   133	
   134	
   135	## How Instructor Enhances Your Workflow
   136	
   137	Instructor introduces three key enhancements compared to direct API usage.
   138	
   139	### Response Model
   140	
   141	Specify a PHP class to extract data into via the 'magic' of LLM chat completion. And that's it.
   142	
   143	Instructor reduces brittleness of the code extracting the information from textual data by leveraging structured LLM responses.
   144	
   145	Instructor helps you write simpler, easier to understand code: you no longer have to define lengthy function call definitions or write code for assigning returned JSON into target data objects.
   146	
   147	### Validation
   148	
   149	Response model generated by LLM can be automatically validated, following set of rules. Currently, Instructor supports only Symfony validation.
   150	
   151	You can also provide a context object to use enhanced validator capabilities.
   152	
   153	### Max Retries
   154	
   155	You can set the number of retry attempts for requests.
   156	
   157	Instructor will repeat requests in case of validation or deserialization error up to the specified number of times, trying to get a valid response from LLM.
   158	
   159	### Support for LLM Providers
   160	
   161	Instructor offers out-of-the-box support for the following LLM providers:
   162	
   163	- A21 / Mamba
   164	- Anthropic
   165	- Azure OpenAI
   166	- Cerebras
   167	- Cohere (v2 OpenAI compatible)
   168	- Deepseek
   169	- Fireworks
   170	- Google Gemini (native and OpenAI compatible)
   171	- Groq
   172	- HuggingFace
   173	- Inception
   174	- Minimaxi
   175	- Mistral
   176	- Moonshot / Kimi
   177	- Ollama (on localhost)
   178	- OpenAI
   179	- OpenRouter
   180	- Perplexity
   181	- Qwen
   182	- Sambanova
   183	- xAI / Grok
   184	
   185	For usage examples, check Hub section or `examples` directory in the code repository.

   197	### Installation
   198	
   199	You can install Instructor via Composer:
   200	
   201	```bash
   202	composer require cognesy/instructor-php
   203	```
   204	
   205	### Basic Example
   206	
   207	This is a simple example demonstrating how Instructor retrieves structured information from provided text (or chat message sequence).
   208	
   209	Response model class is a plain PHP class with typehints specifying the types of fields of the object.
   210	
   211	```php
   212	use Cognesy\Instructor\StructuredOutput;
   213	
   214	// Step 0: Create .env file in your project root:
   215	// OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key
   216	
   217	// Step 1: Define target data structure(s)
   218	class Person {
   219	    public string $name;
   220	    public int $age;
   221	}
   222	
   223	// Step 2: Provide content to process
   224	$text = "His name is Jason and he is 28 years old.";
   225	
   226	// Step 3: Use Instructor to run LLM inference
   227	$person = (new StructuredOutput)
   228	    ->withResponseClass(Person::class)
   229	    ->withMessages($text)
   230	    ->get();
   231	
   232	// Step 4: Work with structured response data
   233	assert($person instanceof Person); // true
   234	assert($person->name === 'Jason'); // true
   235	assert($person->age === 28); // true
   236	
   237	echo $person->name; // Jason
   238	echo $person->age; // 28
   239	
   240	var_dump($person);
   241	// Person {
   242	//     name: "Jason",
   243	//     age: 28
   244	// }    
   245	```
   246	> **NOTE:** Instructor supports classes / objects as response models. In case you want to extract simple types or enums, you need to wrap them in Scalar adapter - see section below: Extracting Scalar Values.
   247	>
   248	
   249	### Validation
   250	
   251	Instructor validates results of LLM response against validation rules specified in your data model.
   252	
   253	> For further details on available validation rules, check [Symfony Validation constraints](https://symfony.com/doc/current/validation.html#constraints).
   254	
   255	```php
   256	use Cognesy\Instructor\StructuredOutput;
   257	use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;
   258	
   259	class Person {
   260	    public string $name;
   261	    #[Assert\PositiveOrZero]
   262	    public int $age;
   263	}
   264	
   265	$text = "His name is Jason, he is -28 years old.";
   266	$person = (new StructuredOutput)
   267	    ->withResponseClass(Person::class)
   268	    ->with(
   269	        messages: [['role' => 'user', 'content' => $text]],
   270	    )
   271	    ->get();
   272	
   273	// if the resulting object does not validate, Instructor throws an exception
   274	```
   275	
   276	
   277	### Max Retries
   278	
   279	In case maxRetries parameter is provided and LLM response does not meet validation criteria, Instructor will make subsequent inference attempts until results meet the requirements or maxRetries is reached.
   280	
   281	Instructor uses validation errors to inform LLM on the problems identified in the response, so that LLM can try self-correcting in the next attempt.
   282	
   283	```php
   284	use Cognesy\Instructor\StructuredOutput;
   285	use Cognesy\Instructor\StructuredOutputRuntime;
   286	use Cognesy\Polyglot\Inference\LLMProvider;
   287	use Symfony\Component\Validator\Constraints as Assert;
   288	
   289	class Person {
   290	    #[Assert\Length(min: 3)]
   291	    public string $name;
   292	    #[Assert\PositiveOrZero]
   293	    public int $age;
   294	}
   295	
   296	$text = "His name is JX, aka Jason, he is -28 years old.";
   297	$runtime = StructuredOutputRuntime::fromProvider(LLMProvider::new())
   298	    ->withMaxRetries(3);
   299	
   300	$person = (new StructuredOutput($runtime))
   301	    ->with(
   302	        messages: [['role' => 'user', 'content' => $text]],
   303	        responseModel: Person::class,
   304	    )
   305	    ->get();
   306	
   307	// if all LLM's attempts to self-correct the results fail, Instructor throws an exception
   308	```
   309	
   310	
   311	### Output Modes
   312	
   313	Instructor supports multiple output modes through `Cognesy\Instructor\Enums\OutputMode` to allow working with various models depending on their capabilities.
   314	- `OutputMode::Json` - generate structured output via LLM's native JSON generation 
   315	- `OutputMode::JsonSchema` - use LLM's strict JSON Schema mode to enforce JSON Schema
